title: Canonical ordinary etale deformation-family fibre and specialization arrows
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring in universe $u+1$, and work with schemes in universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme] and ordinary etale derived categories of constant-$A$ modules [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a compactifiable map $g:V\to S$ and section $s:S\to V$, write $C_A(g,s)=s^*g^\times A_S$, using the ordinary compact-support right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] and exact inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. On the actual extended-Rees deformation with projection $\widetilde g:D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_S$ and augmentation section $\widetilde s$ [def-pur-dnc-section-family], define $F_A=C_A(\widetilde g,\widetilde s)$ whenever $\widetilde g$ is compactifiable. For a Cartesian square $(v,b):(g':V'\to S')\to(g:V\to S)$ with compactifiable vertical maps and quasi-compact $g'$, and compatible sections $s'v=bs$, define the section map $b^*C_A(g,s)\to C_A(g',s')$ by inverse-image composition, then $s'^*$ of the canonical exceptional base-change mate [def-asd-smooth-dualizing-base-change-arrows]. For a closed section with $sg=1_S$, define $\eta_1:i_1^*F_A\to C_A(g,s)$ by this map on the actual one-fibre square. Define $\eta_0:i_0^*F_A\to C_A(\pi_N,0_N)$ on the actual normal-cone fibre square [def-pur-normal-bundle], assuming its projection is compactifiable and quasi-compact. Here $i_1,i_0:S\to\mathbf A^1_S$ and $a:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ are the standard sections and projection [def-sbc-affine-space]. For $\kappa:F_A\simeq a^*C_A(g,s)$ define normalized to mean $i_1^*\kappa$ followed by the canonical section/composition unit equals $\eta_1$. Define specialization as the canonical inverse unit $C_A(g,s)\to i_0^*a^*C_A(g,s)$, followed by $i_0^*(\kappa^{-1})$ and $\eta_0$. For any $b:S'\to S$ and $C\in D(S_{et},A)$, define the line-pullback comparison $\mathbf A^1(b)^*a^*C\simeq a'^*b^*C$ from inverse-image composition and the commuting affine-line projection square. No invertibility, constancy or existence of normalized $\kappa$ is asserted.
